text:
Mark Scheifele now holds a franchise record. Ken Wiebe of the Winnipeg Free Press wrote that after a four-point night and a shootout goal in a comeback win in Chicago, Scheifele "now stands alone as the franchise points leader." Sportsnet followed with "How Scheifele proved doubters wrong and etched name into Jets lore."

He is not slowing down to celebrate. After 103 points last season he has 29 (7 goals) in 23 games, 13 on the power play, at 21.5 minutes a night. His last ten games brought 18 points where we'd expect about 12.7 at his ice time, and the chances with him on are up too. If anything he has been unlucky shooting: 7 goals on 9.2 expected.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season, with 71% of his exits leaving the zone with the puck. The question has always been defense: Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more with him on last season (bottom 3% of forwards), though this year Winnipeg's 5v5 chance share is 8 points better with him than without. Our range for his season is 90 to 119 points.
